action: Universities: check whether admin, deployment and test pages are exposed externally, replace possibly stolen authentication keys and database accounts, and respond jointly with the vendor, as S2W advises.
date_note: Date of the Etnews article relaying S2W's report; the claimed intrusions were 12 to 17 November.
exec: A claimed campaign against Korean universities reportedly used an AI penetration-testing tool; the real scope is not confirmed.
plain: Security firm S2W says a hacker claimed to have breached Korean universities and posted data on Telegram, and that traces point to an AI-based attack tool. The real scope has not been confirmed.
summary: Etnews reports a hacker called KimJEN claimed to have hacked Korean universities and public bodies from 12 to 17 November and posted internal data on Telegram, claiming about 100 universities; the actual scope is not confirmed. S2W found signs of an AI-based penetration-testing tool, and indications of a stolen key and web shell on about 20 universities' rERP systems.
title: S2W: hacker claims Korean university breaches using AI tool; scope unconfirmed

validation.note: One outlet (Etnews, 19 Nov) read in full, relaying S2W's report; the S2W report itself and any university or vendor statement were not read.

review.note: Compared claim status, KimJEN, 12-17 Nov, about 100 universities, about 20 rERP findings, S2W advice and unconfirmed scope against Etnews
